text:
Looking at the diff: `case 'millisecond':` (the singular form, which was supported in ms@2.1.3) has been replaced with `case "":`.

Two observations:

1. **`case "":` is dead code.** The regex group `(milliseconds?|msecs?|ms|...)` can only ever match a non-empty string; when no unit is present, `match[2]` is `undefined` and `(match[2] || 'ms')` yields `'ms'`. So `type` can never be `''`, and this case never fires.

2. **The singular `millisecond` is silently dropped.** Previously `ms('1 millisecond')` matched the regex (`n = 1`, `type = 'millisecond'`) and hit the `case 'millisecond':` label, returning `1`. Now no case matches, so it falls through to `default: return undefined`. Callers observing `ms('5 millisecond')` get `undefined` instead of `5` — the same observable break would apply to `ms('1 millisecond')` used in timeouts, etc.

The library's own suite (`tests.js`) never exercises the singular `millisecond` form (it tests `'100ms'`, `'1s'`, etc.), which is why it stays green despite this change. A test on the singular form fails on the patched build (`undefined` vs `1`) and passes on the original.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "proof-test.js", "content": "var assert = require('assert');\nvar ms = require('./');\n\ndescribe('proof', function () {\n  it('parses the singular millisecond unit', function () {\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('1 millisecond'), 1);\n    assert.strictEqual(ms('50 millisecond'), 50);\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The diff removes the 'millisecond' case label and replaces it with a dead case '' (the regex can never produce an empty unit, since a missing unit becomes 'ms' via the || fallback). As a result ms('1 millisecond') now returns undefined instead of 1, an observable behaviour change that the existing test suite never covers."}
```
